beats.eyebrow: What you were taught
beats.mito: It is crude oil. It suffocates your skin and clogs your pores.
beats.verdad: What is sold in a chemist is refined to a pharmaceutical standard, three times over. The testing says it does not block a pore.

beats.eyebrow: Why it never sinks in
beats.title: It has nowhere to go
beats.body: The molecules are too big to get down into a pore in the first place. It stays on top — which, for a lid, is the entire job description.

beats.title: THE MISTAKE, AND THE FIX

beats.eyebrow: What everybody tells you
beats.mito: Put a good thick layer on. Slather it. More is better.
beats.verdad: A thick layer cannot seal better than a thin one. The seal is made by the first microscopically thin film that touches your skin.

beats.eyebrow: All of the risk, none of the benefit
beats.title: It is not a slather. It is a film.
beats.body: Everything above that first film does nothing at all — it just sits there getting warm, and creeps. The mess, the pillow, the gummed up eye: all of it comes from the part that was never working.

beats.label: Seal bone dry skin and you have sealed the dry IN

beats.eyebrow: That is the whole secret, and it is free

beats.title: The whole thing, in three lines
items: 1 · Rinse and do NOT dry. Leave the skin damp and cool.
2 · A grain of rice, warmed between two fingertips until it goes clear.
3 · Press it along the bone under the eye. Never above it. Every other night.
